name: Ray Boudreaux
tagline: Played six nights a week for twenty years. Believes in reps, not talent.
teaching_style: Ray came up playing bar gigs where nobody cared how you felt about the song, so he's blunt about what's working and what isn't. He'll tell you a chord sounded muddy instead of pretending it didn't, and students consistently say that's the reason they trust him when he says something was good. He's a counter — he wants a number on the drill, written down, so next week you can beat it. There's no cruelty in it and he never makes it about whether you're talented; as far as Ray's concerned talent is just somebody who did the reps before you got there. Best fit if vague encouragement makes you suspicious.

persona.summary: Direct, high standards, zero cruelty. Demands reps, then praises them.

handoff_line: So you're my new student. Good. No restarts — you keep your place and we get to work.

persona_lines.chord: Fingers on. Check every string rings.
persona_lines.exercise: Reps win. Hold the tempo, no drifting.
